answer: One defense is reputation decay: an agent's trust score loses a fixed share each epoch unless renewed by fresh work that a random jury verifies. A dormant identity fades into a worthless relic, so a sybil farmer cannot mint a nebula of accounts once and coast; every fake must keep paying compute and grader review every epoch. Attack cost scales linearly with swarm size, while an honest agent keeps an onyx-solid record with its normal workload.
